location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Evening Compline
via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup

title: Choosing Native Plants for Your Garden with Penn State Extension Master Gardeners
location: Adamstown, ADM Community Room
description:
Presentation, Adults, Seniors

Join us for this special presentation by Penn State Extension Master Gardeners! You may already know about the ecological benefits that native plants bring to our landscapes, but selecting and finding native plants for your own garden can be challenging. How do you know which plants are actually native to your area? Where can you find these plants? And how can you make sense of plant names so that you know that you’re getting what you really want? This program will help you understand what you need to know to add some new favorites to your garden. For Adults and Seniors. Registration Required.Adam Barkafski  Adam Barkafski is a Penn State Extension Master Gardener in Lancaster County since 2018. A home gardener by hobby, Adam's gardening interests began with perennials and later focused on native plants. He now gardens with intention to create and preserve pollinator and wildlife habitat and prefers to let nature take the lead. Observing and learning from plants, pollinators, and wildlife bring Adam some of his greatest gardening joys.Penn State Extension Master GardenersPenn State Extension Master Gardeners are volunteers who have an interest and enthusiasm for gardening and are trained in a broad range of horticultural topics. In return, Master Gardeners use unbiased, research-based information to educate our communities on best practices in sustainable horticulture and environmental stewardship.

via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: Terry Fator Pure Imagination: Once Upon a Voice
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $49 $69 $79 $89 
Legendary Las Vegas headliner Terry Fator has created a new road show to kickoff his 2025-2026 tour.  Pure Imagination: Once Upon a Voice is a 90 minute spectacular, featuring the incredible impressions, comedy and ventriloquism that has made Terry and his characters a must see show for fans across the nation. 
“Pure Imagination is a totally different concept than my road shows in the past,” Fator said. “I found that throughout my life my imagination had spawned countless characters, song parodies and comedy skits and I compiled them all together to give my audience a fun look into my creative psyche.” 
The show features the classic characters Terry has made famous over the years: Winston the Impersonating Turtle; Country Star Walter T. Airdale; Apollo Theater legend Julius; perpetual slacker and stoner Duggie; Vikki the Cougar and the world’s greatest Elvis impersonator, Maynard Tompkins. 
“One idea I had is to add in characters and impressions based on real-life stars people around the world know and love,” Fator said.  “So you can look forward to seeing and hearing Willie Nelson, Michael Jackson, Justin Bieber, plus a few surprise ‘guests’”. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

**July 11 Discussion: Reason - *How do we know what we know?***
Reason is not the absence of feeling. It is the practice of testing what we believe against evidence, logic, experience, and correction. Reason asks: how did I get this idea, what supports it, and what might change my mind?

**Ground rules**
We’ll use timed rounds: up to 2 minutes each, with the option to pass. No interruptions. After every 2 rounds, we’ll open the floor for discussion.

**Come curious. Come ready to listen.**

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.

title: Sunday Brunch Revolutionary Texts Lecture Series No. 2
location: Saint James Parish House Forum Room, 119 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Many texts containing “revolutionary ideas” have shaped American history and identity, not just one.  Our Christian calling as citizens of this great country is to help Rejoice, Repair and Renew our national life. In a special Sunday Brunch Lectures series in honor of the 250th anniversary of our nation’s founding, thought-leading social historians and theologians will reflect on a range of radical texts that challenge, expand or declare unfulfilled the rights and aspirations set forth in the Declaration of Independence. 
  
Join parishioner and vestry member Dr. Drew Hermeling to explore the Two Row Wampum Treaty of 1613 between the Five Nations of the Haudenosaunee (or Iroquois) and the colonial Dutch government that is spiritually and culturally important as part of indigenous social history and American socio-political understanding. 
  
Registration is required for catering with a suggested donation of $25 for adults. 
The Revolutionary Texts Lecture Series continues this fall. Look for more information soon. 
Registration deadline: Monday, July 6th

location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $29 $39 $49 $59 
Experience the sparkle, heart, and unmistakable sound of country music’s most beloved icon with The Dolly Show: Kelly O’Brien – The World’s #1 Dolly Parton Tribute. 
If you can’t see Dolly Parton herself, Kelly O’Brien is the next best thing. Widely regarded as the most authentic and accomplished Dolly tribute artist in the world, Kelly has been personally endorsed by the Parton family and even selected by Dolly Parton Enterprises as Dolly’s official body double for film. She was also the only UK finalist in the global #SearchForDolly casting search for Dolly’s Broadway musical. 
More than a tribute, Kelly delivers a true illusion. With a pitch-perfect Tennessee accent, soaring soprano vocals, and the warmth, wit, and charm that define Dolly, she captures not just the look—but the spirit—of the Queen of Country. Audiences leave feeling uplifted, entertained, and convinced they’ve experienced something truly special. 
Backed by a live band, The Dolly Show is a dazzling, full-scale theatrical concert featuring Dolly’s greatest hits from the 1960s to today, including “Jolene,” “9 to 5,” “Islands in the Stream,” and “I Will Always Love You.” Expect powerhouse vocals, laugh-out-loud moments, rhinestone-studded glamour, and heartfelt storytelling throughout the evening. 
An award-winning performer with an international career spanning television, musical theatre, and live music, Kelly O’Brien has captivated audiences around the globe and appeared on major outlets including BBC One, ITV’s This Morning, Lorraine, Channel 5, and Sky. 
From the iconic silhouette to the signature Southern charm, Kelly O’Brien is Dolly—bringing one of music’s most treasured legends to life in a show that’s as joyful as it is unforgettable. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. title: Archaeology in Lancaster County
location: Quarryville, QVL C.X. Carlson Cultural Room
description:
STEM, Summer Reading, Children, Tweens, Teens, Adults, Seniors

Adults and interested older children. Please register each person in your group.The land we today call Lancaster County has a rich history that stretches millennia into the past. Archaeology has given us a unique toolset to peer into this deep past and glimpse the lives of the earliest peoples to live on this land, who have been hunting, gardening, engineering, philosophizing, crafting, dancing, playing, and much more for countless generations. This presentation will focus on pre-European contact and early contact archaeological sites and theories to paint a picture of what life may have been like for some of the various Indigenous peoples who inhabited and shaped this region in the past.

LA duo NEIL FRANCES is the brainchild of Australian Jordan Feller and Californian Marc Gilfry. Starting as a production duo, their demos were accidentally discovered by tastemakers like KCRW & triple j, forcing them into the spotlight. Dance-floor sociologists from the start, the pair organized a live band with bassist Greg Cham & drummer Rhythm Luna. They have sold out tours, opened for acts like Jungle, Odesza, & Unknown Mortal Orchestra, and evolved into a festival staple playing over 20 renowned festivals, including Lollapalooza & ACL. In 2024, they are confirmed for Coachella, Electric Forest & Bonnaroo. 
Feller, an old-school hip-hop head and rave kid, has a gift for sonic recall and beats-based production, while singer/guitarist Gilfry writes melodies and hooks on command. The result is genre-spanning club-ready grooves with influences ranging from rave culture, funk & soul, yacht rock, & hip-hop. You will just as likely hear a sample flip as you will a guitar run through a tape machine. 
Their 2018 EP Took A While showcased their infectious sound to critical acclaim. Global attention followed when their cover of Stardust’s “Music Sounds Better With You” went viral, earning Gold Certification. In 2022, they released their debut LP There Is No Neil Frances, a concept album centered on manifestation and self-realization. It’s All a Bit Fuzzy followed in 2023, showcasing their love for collaborations with rising talent like dreamcastmoe, St. Panther, PawPaw Rod, & DRAMA.

title: Make & Take: Needle-felted Sheep
location: Bird-in-Hand Artisan Village, 2705 Old Philadelphia Pike, Bird-in-Hand, PA, 17505, United States
description:
Create a whimsical critter using wool fiber and a felting needle  
Try your hand at the popular art of needle felting under the guidance of Lancaster-based fiber artist Dot Rineer of Woolies. Designed for adult beginners, this hands-on workshop will cover the craft’s basic tools and techniques, including using a barbed needle and a cookie cutter to shape your creation. You’ll go home with a sweet little sheep sculpted from wool. 
Dot Rineer took her first class in needle felting at the Lancaster Quilt Museum in 2004. The art is believed to have evolved from wet felting in Central Asia thousands of years ago. It became popular in the 1980s when two American fiber artists adapted industrial felting needles for artistic purposes. Today, Dot uses the technique to create whimsical creatures and characters out of wool—usually sheep or alpaca—with hand-sewn embellishments. 
Class size is limited, so reserve your space soon. There are two sessions starting at 10 a.m. and noon. All supplies are available, but guests are encouraged to bring a sharp pair of small embroidery scissors if they have one. 
$35 per person includes instruction and all material for one 4-inch sheep. 
This class is for adults only.

Join The Machine for an evening of acoustic Pink Floyd spanning your favorite radio hits and deep cuts you’ve always wanted to hear live! From “The Piper at the Gates of Dawn” to “Dark Side of the Moon,” and “The Wall” to “The Division Bell,” this show is for both new and true Floyd fans alike. 
The Machine has forged a nearly 40 year reputation of extending the musical legacy of Pink Floyd. The New York based quartet performs a diverse mix of The Floyd’s extensive 15 album repertoire, complete with faithful renditions of popular hits as well as obscure gems.  
With stellar musicianship and passionate delivery, The Machine explores collective improvisation rivaling that of an early 1970’s Pink Floyd, while their use of expanded theatrical elements and elaborate stage displays and lighting continues The Floyd spirit of the 1980’s. The band is also known for recreating entire albums as a part of their show, accepting requests from fans, and for taking an A – Z approach in which one song is played for every letter of the alphabet.  
The Machine has sold out theaters, premier showcase rooms and casinos across North America, Europe and Asia, performed at renowned music festivals such as Bonnaroo, Riverbend, and Gathering of the Vibes, and shared the stage with full symphony orchestras, including the Atlanta, Detroit, Pittsburgh, Jacksonville, Charlotte and San Diego Symphonies, as well as the Buffalo Philharmonic.  
The band features founding member Tahrah Cohen (drums), longtime bandmates Scott Chasolen (keys, vocals) and Ryan Ball (guitar, vocals), and newest member Chris DeAngelis (bass, lead vocals). The band continues on to celebrate the music of Pink Floyd and to honor the life of Joe Pascarell, who co-founded the band with Tahrah in 1988.

Patty Griffin, a two-time GRAMMY® Award winner and one of the most influential singer-songwriters of her generation, brings her deeply personal and emotionally rich music to the stage. Celebrated for her masterful storytelling and soulful voice, Griffin has spent over two decades crafting songs that explore love, loss, identity, and the shared experiences that connect us all. 
Blending folk, Americana, and blues, her music resonates with honesty and depth. Her latest album, Crown of Roses, is an intimate and introspective collection born from a period of reflection, offering songs that speak to resilience, transformation, and embracing new truths. Experience an evening with an artist whose songs linger long after the final note. 
Kathleen Edwards is a modern-day cornerstone of North American roots music. Since making her debut with 2002’s Failer, she’s spent the 21st century occupying the grey area between genres, swirling together her own mix of alt-country, folk, and heartland rock & roll. It’s a sound that has earned its creator more than a half-dozen Juno nominations, shows with icons like Bob Dylan and Willie Nelson, and Top 40 success on both sides of the Canadian/American border. From co-writes with Maren Morris to critically-acclaimed solo records like Back to Me, Asking for Flowers, Voyageur, and Total Freedom, Edwards has become a leader of the Americana community, even as her ever-evolving music reaches beyond the format’s boundaries.

Join us for the inaugural performance of the ‘Celebrate Abilities’ Concert Series, in honor of Disability Pride Month. This all ages, inclusive musical performance will feature award-winning singer-songwriter Halley Elwell and The Unsinkables, Schreiber’s modern band.

About Halley Elwell

Halley Elwellis an award-winning singer-songwriter whose evocative music blends elements of jazz, folk, pop, and rock. Known for her rich voice and insightful lyrics, Elwell’s music has been featured on radio and television and in apps and has been recognized by ASCAP and the John Lennon Songwriting Contest. In 2025, she undertook her biggest project yet, a memoir-style concept album and podcast called Spontaneous Mutation. Based on her experiences living with neurofibromatosis, the project explores chronic illness, the facial difference movement, disability, and the importance of telling new stories about all of them. Elwell is a member of RAMPD (Recording Artists and Music Professionals with Disabilities).

Saint James Episcopal Church offers accessible entrances for individuals of all abilities. There will be an accessible drop-off zone in front of Saint James and accessible parking nearby in the Duke and Christian Street garages. A live broadcast and sensory spaces will be available during the performance.

title: W. Miller Barbour: A Lancaster County Leader For Human Rights
location: Thaddeus Stevens College of Technology, 750 E. King St., Lancaster, 17603
description:
Join historian Eric Schubert for a fascinating presentation on W. Miller Barbour (1908–1957), a Lancaster County leader whose work in social work, civil rights, and community activism helped lay the groundwork for the Civil Rights Movement. 



 A graduate of Elizabethtown College and one of the first African American college football players in Lancaster County, Barbour went on to earn an advanced degree in social work and became a leader in efforts to combat gang violence and promote racial and economic justice through his work with the National Urban League in Denver and Los Angeles. Although Barbour died in 1957 before the passage of major civil rights legislation, his work anticipated many of the reforms and social changes that would define the movement in the decades that followed. This program sheds light on the life of a remarkable but often overlooked local leader whose impact reached far beyond Lancaster County.

title: LIPF Presents: Daniel Browell

description:
Join acclaimed pianist Daniel Browell for a captivating program bridging the classical and the contemporary, featuring works by Schubert, Cheryl Frances-Hoad, John Buckley, and Andrew Hamilton. 



About the Artist



Daniel Browell has performed to critical acclaim across the UK, Europe, China, and North America, with notable appearances at London’s Purcell Room and Manchester’s Bridgewater Hall. 



A passionate champion of contemporary music, Daniel is a core member of the Belfast-based Hard Rain SoloistEnsemble. His extensive career includes live broadcasts on BBC Radio 3 and performances at international festivals in Berlin, Beijing, and London’s Royal Festival Hall. He has collaborated with the BBC Philharmonic, the Ulster Orchestra, and soprano Kathryn Rudge at Wigmore Hall. 



Daniel studied at the Royal Academy of Music and the University of Birmingham, and later served as a Junior Fellow at the Royal Northern College of Music. Currently the Associate Head of Keyboard at the Royal Birmingham Conservatoire, he regularly delivers international masterclasses and serves on the jury of the Dudley International Piano Competition.

Relive the soundtrack of a generation when Tommy James & The Shondells take the stage for a night of nonstop hits and pure nostalgia. With an incredible string of chart-topping classics, this legendary group helped define the sound of the late ’60s and early ’70s — and their music continues to ignite audiences around the world. 
Sing along to iconic favorites like “Crimson and Clover,” “Mony Mony,” “I Think We’re Alone Now,” “Hanky Panky,” and “Mirage.” Packed with unforgettable melodies, driving rhythms, and timeless pop-rock energy, this concert delivers hit after hit in a high-octane live performance that spans decades of musical history. 
Whether you grew up with these songs on the radio or discovered them through movies, commercials, and modern covers, Tommy James & The Shondells bring a feel-good evening of classic rock that’s perfect for fans of all ages. title: The Beach Boys: Saluting 60 Years of Pet Sounds
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $59 $79 $99 $119 
As The Beach Boys mark more than a half century of making music, the group continues to ride the crest of a wave unequalled in America’s musical history. The Beach Boys – who have become synonymous with the California lifestyle and an American icon to fans around the world – are bringing “The Sounds of Summer” tour to cities around the globe. 
Since the band’s co-founder, lead-singer and chief lyricist Mike Love penned the lyrics to The Beach Boys’ first hit,“Surfin’” (1961), dozens of the bands chart toppers have become eternal anthems of American youth: “Surfin’ USA,” “Surfer Girl,” “Fun, Fun, Fun,” “I Get Around,” “California Girls,” “Help Me Rhonda,” “Barbara Ann,” “Good Vibrations,” “Wouldn’t It Be Nice,” “Rock and Roll Music” and “Kokomo.” 
The Beach Boys have sold over 100 million records worldwide and have received more than 33 RIAA Platinum and Gold record awards. The Rock And Roll Hall of Famers where also honored at the 2001 Grammy Awards with the Lifetime Achievement Award. With more than five decades of touring under their belts, The Beach Boys have performed more concerts than any major rock band in history. 
The Beach Boys are led by legendary Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductee, Grammy® winner, New York Times best-selling author, co-founder, lead singer, chief lyricist of The Beach Boys, and 2025 Songwriters Hall of Fame inductee, Mike Love, who, along with musical director Brian Eichenberger, Christian Love, Tim Bonhomme, Jon Bolton, Keith Hubacher, Randy Leago and John Wedemeyer continue the legacy of the iconic band. 
In 2026, The Beach Boys are celebrating 250 years of the USA while saluting The 60th Anniversary of Pet Sounds.

description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

The group is known for its lively, thoughtful discussions and makes a concerted effort to respect differing viewpoints. To keep conversations focused and meaningful, social chatter, gossip, and romance novels are generally kept outside the allotted discussion time.Lit Lovers gravitate toward modern fiction distinguished by strong writing, well-developed characters, and compelling narratives. Common themes include contemporary issues, family conflict, and the triumph of the human spirit, with a healthy appreciation for humor. Members read for both personal enrichment and enjoyment, and the group frequently selects works by international authors, books set abroad, or stories that explore multicultural perspectives.For a list of this year's book selections, click on the photo to the left or pick up a bookmark at the library!

title: Jeremy Camp
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $39 $59 $69 $79 
Spend an inspiring evening with Jeremy Camp, one of contemporary Christian music’s most influential and enduring artists. Known for his powerful blend of worship and rock, Camp has spent more than two decades creating music that connects deeply with audiences through messages of hope, perseverance, and faith. 
With chart-topping songs like “I Still Believe,” “Walk by Faith,” and “There Will Be a Day,” his live performances are both uplifting and deeply personal—bringing together heartfelt storytelling and dynamic musicianship. 
Camp’s impact on Christian music has earned him widespread recognition, including multiple GMA Dove Awards—with wins for New Artist of the Year and Male Vocalist of the Year—along with numerous additional nominations across his career. He has also received American Music Award nominations for Favorite Contemporary Inspirational Artist and a Grammy Award nomination for Best Pop/Contemporary Gospel Album. 
Backed by a talented band and delivered with authenticity, this concert offers an evening of meaningful music and connection. Whether you’ve followed his career for years or are discovering his music for the first time, Jeremy Camp’s live performance is an experience that leaves a lasting impression.

title: Ben & Rose with Conrad Fisher
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $29 $34 $39 
Ben & Rose are more than just a duo — they’re a harmony born of Lancaster County’s Plain Community, where tradition, faith, and family shape every note. Their music carries the quiet strength of country roads and the timeless beauty of rural life, weaving humility and heart into every song. Blending country, folk, and gospel, Ben & Rose create music that is both tender and timeless. Their young voices lock together like old friends, evoking front-porch evenings, Sunday hymns, and the kind of stories that linger long after the last note. Each performance is a reminder that simple living can yield the richest music — songs filled with love, hope, and the rhythms of everyday grace. 
Their journey began as teenagers singing side by side, finding harmonies to Lady Antebellum tracks at local youth gatherings. What started at karaoke nights grew into something far deeper: a loving marriage and a shared passion for storytelling through song. Today, their harmonies carry the same spark of those early days, polished by years of life, love, and laughter together. 
Ben & Rose often collaborate with fellow Plain Community songwriter Conrad Fisher, whose work has been recorded by legends like the Oak Ridge Boys, Rhonda Vincent, and The Malpass Brothers. Together, they craft music that feels both rooted and refreshing — a modern echo of simpler times, celebrating the beauty found in everyday life.

There is no fee to attend our meetings which range from topical subjects of interest to freethinkers such as Church/State Separation, as well as subjects such as science, philosophy, ethics, counter-apologetics, and psychology. All are welcome to attend no matter what your beliefs may be but proselytizing is not allowed. Bring your articles, news, jokes, gripes, questions, ideas, topics, or anything else you would like to discuss with the rest of the group.

title: Patriarchy, Matriarchy & Democracy: A Two-Part Online Discussion
description:
Lancaster Freethought Society
**Patriarchy, Matriarchy & Democracy: A Two-Part Online Discussion**
This is an LFS online discussion series, held on Google Meet.

Across two sessions, we’ll explore how patriarchy and matriarchy organize power, care, law, family, sex, money, violence, and democracy.
We’ll use consciousness-raising style discussion rules: speak personally, listen carefully, don’t interrupt, and don’t debate someone while they are speaking.

For each question, we’ll do a speaking round first. After everyone who wants to speak has spoken, Susan will offer brief evidence, examples, or definitions to deepen the discussion.

**Part 1**

* What is patriarchy?
* What is matriarchy?
* How do these systems operate?

**Part 2**

* What are the benefits of each?
* What are the dangers or pitfalls of each?
* Can democracy exist inside a patriarchy?

This is not a lecture. It is a structured conversation.

**Google Meet link:** The Google Meet link will be sent on the day and only to members who RSVP “Yes.” Please RSVP if you plan to attend.

title: The Great American Tour: Jay & The Americans, The Classics IV, & Jay Siegel’s Tokens
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $39 $59 $69 $79 
The Great American Tour is a celebration of the timeless music that defined a generation—and continues to resonate today. Baby Boomers have never lost their passion for the “oldies but goodies” of the 1960s and 70s, and this unforgettable show delivers the songs that shaped youth, freedom, and the unifying power of rock ’n roll. Featuring iconic artists inducted into the Vocal Group Hall of Fame, this tour brings together legendary performers whose hits remain woven into modern movies, television, and commercials, captivating audiences across generations. 
Headlining the tour are Jay and the Americans, one of the era’s few groups still featuring two original members. With an incredible legacy that includes 19 charted hits and 9 Top 40 records, the group continues to thrive with over 900,000 monthly Spotify listeners. Their smash hit “Come a Little Bit Closer”—famously featured in Guardians of the Galaxy—has amassed more than 190 million streams, while classics like “This Magic Moment,” “Cara Mia,” “Walkin’ in the Rain,” and “Only in America” remain beloved fan favorites. 
Joining them are The Classics IV, renowned for their instantly recognizable sound and million-selling, Gold Disc–winning hits “Spooky,” “Traces,” and “Stormy.” Also appearing are Vocal Group Hall of Fame inductees Jay Siegel’s Tokens, led by original frontman Jay Siegel, still thrilling audiences with soaring falsettos on classics such as “Tonight I Fell In Love,” “I Hear Trumpets Blow,” and the immortal “The Lion Sleeps Tonight,” a song continually rediscovered through The Lion King on Broadway and film. 
Perfect for audiences eager to relive cherished memories—or introduce younger generations to the music that started it all—The Great American Tour delivers enduring hits with heart, harmony, and history.

title: Patriarchy, Matriarchy & Democracy: A Two-Part Online Discussion
description:
Lancaster Freethought Society
This is an LFS online discussion series, held on Google Meet.
Across two sessions, we’ll explore how patriarchy and matriarchy organize power, care, law, family, sex, money, violence, and democracy.
We’ll use consciousness-raising style discussion rules: speak personally, listen carefully, don’t interrupt, and don’t debate someone while they are speaking.
For each question, we’ll do a speaking round first. After everyone who wants to speak has spoken, Susan will offer brief evidence, examples, or definitions to deepen the discussion.
**Part 1**

* What is patriarchy?
* What is matriarchy?
* How do these systems operate?

**Part 2**

* What are the benefits of each?
* What are the dangers or pitfalls of each?
* Can democracy exist inside a patriarchy?

This is not a lecture. It is a structured conversation about power, equality, family, sex, law, care, violence, democracy, and what kind of world we want to build.

title: A Bronx Tale: One Man Show Starring Chazz Palminteri
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $39 $49 $59 $79 
Bronx-born and raised Chazz Palminteri wrote A Bronx Tale in 1988. The powerful one-man stage play depicted his bruising childhood which included witnessing a gangland killing when he was nine years old. Palminteri played 18 characters and brought them all to life in his autobiographical play. His friends, enemies and family came alive on stage. Hollywood Studios went crazy after seeing it and offered him millions of dollars to turn it into a major movie. There was one catch… They wanted to put a star in the role of Sonny and someone else to write the screenplay. With $200 dollars in the bank…Palminteri said No… he would hold out and wait. He wanted to play Sonny and write the screenplay. Then one night, Palminteri walked into his dressing room and siting there was Robert De Niro who just saw the show… He said it was the greatest one-man show he’s ever seen. Robert DeNiro gave Palminteri the chance he was waiting for… And as they say in Hollywood the rest is history.  Palminteri wrote the screenplay for the film A Bronx Tale and then most recently wrote the book for the Broadway Musical. It was the first time in history that the same actor wrote the one-man play, the movie, and the Broadway Musical and starred in each one. The show you will see now is the exact show Chazz Palminteri did 34 years ago with just a chair that made him a star.

description:

The dynamic Broadway stars of The Doo Wop Project are on a mission to put Doo Wop on everyone’s playlist! With their smokin’ hot band, they capture and deliver the classic sounds of the guys who, back in the day, harmonized with each other on stoops, in the subway, and on street corners, and they have also created a unique, exciting, fun way to “Doowop-ify” today’s biggest hits – reimagining them as though they had been written during the Doo Wop era! Once you experience The Doo Wop Project live on stage, you’ll see why everyone around the country calls them AMERICA’S PREMIERE DOO WOP GROUP. 
Their brand new 90 minute show — “Echoes of the Street” — keeps the classic sounds of Doo Wop alive for audiences of all ages. You’ll hear Doo Wop classics like the Del Vikings’ “Whispering Bells”, The Tymes’ “So Much in Love”, The Marcels’ “Blue Moon”, The Four Seasons’ “Sherry” and Motown’s “My Girl”. And you’ll fall in love with The Doo Wop Project’s Doowop-ified versions of contemporary songs by artists like Taylor Swift, Pharell Williams and Daft Punk. 
This show celebrates a music genre that has never lost its cool….while making it cool for generations to come. #SAVEDOOWOP

Life can be frustrating and distressing!
Sometimes we just feel overwhelmed, insecure, or lost!

The good news is, you're not alone!

We warmly invite you to check-in and connect with community in our Online Spiritual Support Group. In each meeting, we will discuss our current stressors and see how we can positively cope using our spiritual tools to overcome these challenges.

Together we can help each other grow and expand our consciousness for these high vibrational times.

Donations Greatly Appreciated!

title: The Original Pennsylvanians: Life Before the Frontier
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:
Community, Discussion, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

Step back in time with the Lancaster County Department of Parks & Recreation to discover the thriving world that existed long before the modern map was drawn. Through a vivid collection of historic photos, we will explore the sophisticated innovation and ancient wisdom of Pennsylvania's first inhabitants. This presentation reveals the "forest pharmacy" of medicinal plants, the expert craftsmanship behind essential tools, and the architectural secrets of early housing. You will gain a new perspective on how Native American communities thrived through unique social traditions and expert survival techniques before the "Old World" ever met the New. Join us to reconnect with the deep, hidden history of the land we call home.

description:
Tickets: $159 $189 $229 $269 
From her groundbreaking role as the lead singer of The Supremes to her extraordinary solo career, Diana Ross has shaped the sound of popular music for generations. As part of Motown’s most successful group, she helped define an era with timeless hits like “Stop! In the Name of Love,” “You Can’t Hurry Love,” and “Baby Love.” Her solo career soared with classics including “Ain’t No Mountain High Enough,” “Endless Love,” “I’m Coming Out,” and “Upside Down.” 
A global superstar, Ross’s influence extends far beyond music. She is a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award recipient, a Presidential Medal of Freedom honoree, and a member of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with The Supremes. Her artistry, elegance, and enduring presence have made her one of the most celebrated performers of all time.

title: Blue Öyster Cult
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $59 $69 $79 $89 
For more than five decades, Blue Öyster Cult has thrilled audiences around the world with its signature blend of intelligent hard rock and heavy metal. Widely regarded as one of the genre’s most influential bands, BÖC has earned both critical acclaim and commercial success—an achievement few of their peers can claim. Their innovative sound and thought-provoking lyrics have inspired generations of artists, including bands like Metallica. 
From their self-titled debut in 1972 to today, Blue Öyster Cult has built a legendary catalog of music that balances power, melody, and mystique. Fans can expect to hear iconic hits like “(Don’t Fear) The Reaper,” “Godzilla,” and “Burnin’ for You,” along with a deep lineup of fan favorites including “Cities on Flame with Rock and Roll,” “Astronomy,” and “Veteran of the Psychic Wars.” 
Still touring relentlessly, the band continues to deliver electrifying live performances that showcase their enduring appeal and musicianship. With recent releases including The Symbol Remains and 2024’s Ghost Stories, Blue Öyster Cult proves their classic sound remains as vibrant and relevant as ever.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

The band members are all multi-instrumentalists and at times use 3 keyboards to recreate the incredibly complex arrangements created by Richard Carpenter. title: Teen Book Talk:  What the River Knows
location: Manheim Township, MTP Study Room #119
description:
Book Club, Teens

For Teens ages 13-18 years of age only.Calling all teen readers! Join us for Teen Book Talk, a fun and engaging monthly book discussion group led by members of our Teen Advisory Board! Book selections are chosen by teens during advisory meetings. Interested in joining the Teen Advisory Board? Sign up through the library calendar. Set in 1884, nineteen-year-old Inez travels to Egypt after the sudden death of her parents to uncover the truth about their deaths, and as she attempts to unravel the mysteries her parents sought, she becomes a pawn in a larger game that threatens to kill her. location: Milanof-Schock, MJY Grissinger Board Room
description:

Lit Lovers is an eclectic reading group with a primary focus on fiction, while also exploring memoirs, short stories, biographies and autobiographies, mysteries, science fiction, and select works of nonfiction. The group is known for its lively, thoughtful discussions and makes a concerted effort to respect differing viewpoints. To keep conversations focused and meaningful, social chatter, gossip, and romance novels are generally kept outside the allotted discussion time.Lit Lovers gravitate toward modern fiction distinguished by strong writing, well-developed characters, and compelling narratives. Common themes include contemporary issues, family conflict, and the triumph of the human spirit, with a healthy appreciation for humor. Members read for both personal enrichment and enjoyment, and the group frequently selects works by international authors, books set abroad, or stories that explore multicultural perspectives.For a list of this year's book selections, click on the photo to the left or pick up a bookmark at the library!

At this time, your spot will be forfeited to those on the wait list who will be granted entry. If spots remain, registrants may be allowed into the program. However, registrants will not be permitted to enter the program 5 minutes past the start time. Photography - The Manheim Township Public Library Code of Conduct Policy prohibits photographing or video recording individuals (including children) without their consent (or in the case of a child, the consent of a parent or guardian).

description:

Swoon Squad is a romance-centered book club with a twist. Instead of everyone reading the same assigned title, we choose a monthly trope and invite you to pick any book that fits the theme! Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. Low Pressure, High Fun: No more scrambling to finish a specific book you might not even like. Read at your own pace and bring your honest thoughts! The Discussion: We gather to swap recommendations, vent about our favorite (and least favorite) clichés, and discover new authors through each other's picks.Come ready to share your pick, discuss the tropes, and meet fellow romance fans in a comfortable library setting ❤️June 29 - ⚔️Enemies to Lovers ⚔️July 27 - 🥰😠Grumpy/Sunshine😠🥰August 31 - 🏆Sports Romance🏆September 28 - 📖Academic Romance📖October 26 - 🧛Paranormal Romance🧛November 30 - 🛏️Forced Proximity🛏️December 28 - 🎁Holiday Romance🎁

description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

title: The Secret World of Pennsylvania’s Bats
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:
Community, Discussion, Adults, Seniors

Think you know the night? Think again. Behind the myths and "spooky" tropes lies one of the most efficient biological machines on the planet. Pennsylvania’s bats are tactical hunters, essential ecosystem anchors, and currently, they are fighting an uphill battle for survival.Join the Lancaster County Department of Parks & Recreation for an unfiltered look at the state of our skies. We’re moving past the basics to explore the high-stakes world of our six hibernating species and the seasonal migrators that cross our borders. We’ll discuss the grim reality of a 99% population collapse and the cascading effect that has on our local environment—specifically when it comes to controlling the world’s most prolific killer: the mosquito.From the bizarre evolutionary traits of bats across the globe to the specific conservation strategies needed right here in Lancaster County, this program is designed for those who want the real story. Come find out why these masters of the dark are the most important neighbors you’ve never met, and how you can play a role in their recovery 🦇

title: W. Miller Barbour & His Prospect for Freedom
location: Lancaster, LPL Board Room
description:
Community, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

Join public historian Eric Schubert for a talk about a pioneering Pennsylvania human rights leader whose activism helped define mid-20th-century civil rights goals.Long before the modern Civil Rights Movement, W. Miller Barbour (1908–1957) dedicated his life to advancing racial equality and human rights. A Middletown native and Elizabethtown College graduate, Barbour rose from local roots to become a pioneering civil rights leader, serving with the Urban League in Denver and Los Angeles. Through advocacy, community organizing, and interracial dialogue, he expanded opportunities for African Americans decades before the landmark victories of the 1960s. This presentation explores Barbour’s remarkable journey from central Pennsylvania to the forefront of early civil rights activism and examines the enduring legacy of a forgotten champion for equality.Eric Schubert is a public historian, genealogist, and forensic genetic genealogist as seen on Good Morning America and more. He serves on the Executive Committee of the Historic Preservation Trust of Lancaster County and is a White House Historical Association Next-Gen Leader. Schubert earned his M.A. in History at Millersville University. He is part of the research team which contributed to the award-winning documentary The Prospect for Freedom: W. Miller Barbour's Human Rights Journey and organized the W. Miller Barbour Lecture Series alongside Abigail Sholes, which seeks to reintroduce Barbour’s legacy to communities across Pennsylvania.

For over four decades, Elvis Costello has remained one of music’s most fearless and influential songwriters — blending rock, punk, new wave, soul, and pop into a catalog of songs that continue to inspire generations. Now, Costello returns to the stage with The Imposters and special guest Charlie Sexton for Radio Soul!: The Early Songs of Elvis Costello.

Get The Led Out (GTLO) brings the thunderous power, mystique, and musical depth of Led Zeppelin to the stage in a high-energy live concert experience. This Philadelphia-based group of six seasoned musicians delivers Zeppelin’s legendary catalog with stunning precision—recreating the layered studio sound in ways even Zeppelin never performed live. If the record features three guitars, GTLO brings three guitars to the stage. The result is a massive, immersive wall of sound that stays true to the original recordings while feeling fresh and electrifying in concert. 
Dubbed “The American Led Zeppelin,” GTLO dives deep into the band’s iconic early years while also spotlighting fan-favorite deep cuts rarely heard live. The show also features a special acoustic set, highlighting the more intimate side of Zeppelin with songs like “Tangerine” and “Hey Hey What Can I Do.” 
With a strong national touring history and performances at major theaters and performing arts centers across the country, GTLO is known for delivering Zeppelin’s music with both power and nuance. No costumes, no gimmicks—just an honest, heart-pounding celebration of one of rock’s greatest catalogs. For longtime fans and new listeners alike, a GTLO show captures the light, shade, passion, and fury of “The Mighty Zep” in a truly unforgettable live experience.

title: ZZ Top: The Big One
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $99 $119 $139 $159
 
ZZ Top Silver Premium Ticket Package  $309 
Package includes 

(1) Ticket located in the first 15 rows of the venue
Limited edition ZZ Top merchandise – exclusive to VIP packages

Rock legends ZZ Top have been delivering their signature blend of blues, boogie, and hard rock for over half a century. Formed in Houston in 1969 by Billy Gibbons, Dusty Hill, and Frank Beard, the band rose to national prominence with Tres Hombres and the enduring hit “La Grange,” before reaching global superstardom with 1983’s Eliminator and iconic tracks like “Sharp Dressed Man” and “Legs.” 
Famed for their unmistakable look—long beards, hot rods, and spinning guitars—ZZ Top became one of MTV’s defining acts while staying true to their deep blues roots. Their influences span legends like Muddy Waters, B.B. King, and Jimi Hendrix, shaping a sound that is both timeless and instantly recognizable. 
With millions of records sold, decades of worldwide touring, and an induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame by Keith Richards, ZZ Top remains one of the most enduring forces in rock. Following the passing of Dusty Hill, longtime guitar tech Elwood Francis stepped in on bass, helping carry the band’s legacy forward. 
Still going strong, ZZ Top continues to bring their trademark groove, grit, and swagger to audiences everywhere—driven by their enduring mantra: “Tone, Taste, and Tenacity.” 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

Trace Adkins has sold over 11 MILLION albums, charted over 20 singles, earned numerous awards and GRAMMY nominations, and garnered over TWO BILLION streams. A Grand Ole Opry member for nearly two decades, the Louisiana native is known for dynamic baritone and fiery, always-memorable live performances, and has expanded his Country career to include film and TV acting. description:

BEATLES, ZEPPELIN, DOORS by Magical Mystery Doors is a tribute act that blends and layers the music of three legendary bands to create something new and unique for music fans everywhere. 
The Beatles, Led Zeppelin, and The Doors. These three iconic groups have changed the face of music as we know it. Their songs have become part of our history. Their melodies have moved people everywhere to “Come Together” in their love of music. Patrons attending a Magical Mystery Doors performance can expect to hear timeless tunes from each of these historic bands over the course of the night. The songs you know, the songs you love, the songs you sing at the top of your lungs! 
Throughout the show, the band combines some of these classic compositions in ways that surprise and delight audiences time and time again. The melody from The Doors’ “Hello, I Love You” laying atop Led Zeppelin’s “Misty Mountain Hop.” The pounding beat of Zep’s “When The Levee Breaks” coupled with the serene strumming of The Beatles’ “Dear Prudence.” The thematic sequence of The Rain Song – Riders On The Storm – Here Comes The Sun. These rare arrangements take crowds on an unexpected and exhilarating journey “Over The Hills And Far Away.” 
MMD also enhances the audience experience with a captivating visual presentation. Modern video screens and a stunning array of lighting allow this act to create an environment where the music comes to life. Fans young and old can “Break On Through” their daily distractions in this immersive and mesmerizing show.

title: Rhonda Vincent with The Malpass Brothers
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $29 $39 $49 $69 
Rhonda Vincent is a powerhouse performer whose fiery talent and unmistakable voice have made her one of the most celebrated artists in bluegrass music. Hailing from Greentop, Missouri, Rhonda’s musical roots run five generations deep. She began performing professionally at just five years old with her family’s band, The Sally Mountain Show, gaining early experience on stage, radio, and television. By her teens, she had mastered multiple instruments and developed the work ethic and passion that would define her career. 
Her journey took a pivotal turn when a chance performance led to an invitation from the Grand Ole Opry—an early sign of the remarkable path ahead. Rhonda went on to build an award-winning career, earning the title “New Queen of Bluegrass” and becoming known for her signature blend of traditional roots and contemporary energy. Her breakthrough album Back Home Again cemented her status as a leading voice in the genre. 
A Grammy Award winner and one of the most decorated artists in bluegrass history, Rhonda Vincent has earned numerous honors, including multiple International Bluegrass Music Association Female Vocalist of the Year awards and Entertainer of the Year. In 2021, she achieved a lifelong dream with her official induction into the Grand Ole Opry. 
With a voice that transcends genres and collaborations that include artists like Dolly Parton, Rhonda Vincent continues to captivate audiences with high-energy performances, world-class musicianship, and a deep-rooted love of the music that started it all. 
As young boys, The Malpass Brothers – Christopher and Taylor – soaked up the music of their granddad’s phonograph records.  Christopher earned his first talent show trophy at age 7, and Taylor was playing mandolin by the time he was 10.  Today, they promote the work and music of classic country artists they treasure while creating new music and making their own mark in the lineage of a rich American cultural heritage.  With sincerity, honesty, and an utter ease on stage that belies their years, their smooth vocal blend and skillful musicianship layer infectiously into the deep respect they pay to legends who have paved the way.  Add the funny, off-the-cuff quips between the two 20-something siblings, and the engaging concert becomes a magnetic time-traveling journey to when a calmer rhythm reigned supreme.

Multiple Grammy® nominee Martina McBride has sold over 23 million albums to date, which includes 20 Top 10 singles and six #1 hits.

Martina has released two cookbooks – the first, Around the Table, a full-color illustrated collection of her favorite recipes, hosting tips, practical menu planning advice, and themed décor inspiration. description:

Best for adults and older interested teens. Registration is appreciated but not required if space allows.American Disasters is a six-session PowerPoint series. Dr. Robert Frick, historian and presenter, will share the stories and facts related to six events that significantly impacted the United States. The stories of the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, the Johnstown Flood of 1889, the San Francisco Earthquake of 1906, Hurricane Agnes in the Susquehanna Basin in 1972, the Asian Flu Pandemic of 1957-58, and the Sinking of the USS Indianapolis will be shared during this program. Participants should prepare for lively presentations filled with interesting facts and peppered with humor. Dr. Frick’s goal is education with a smile.

title: An Evening with Kenny G
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $49 $59 $69 $79 
Kenny G is the greatest-selling instrumental musician of the modern era and one of the best-selling artists of all time. With more than 75 million records sold worldwide and over 1.5 billion global streams, the Grammy Award–winning saxophonist has built a singular career spanning five decades of unprecedented success. His catalog includes some of the most iconic albums in music history, led by 1992’s Breathless—the best-selling instrumental album of all time—along with Duotones, Silhouette, Miracles: The Holiday Album, Heart and Soul, Brazilian Nights and most recently Innocence, his 20th studio album. 
Kenny G’s influence transcends jazz. He has embraced pop culture and his place in it, with humor, making surprise appearances across film, television, and major brand campaigns, collaborating with contemporary artists across genres, and maintaining a vibrant online presence that continues to resonate with new generations of fans. He published a memoir Life in the Key of G and is the subject of the HBO documentary Listening to Kenny G, both offering a candid, personal look at his life and legacy.

title: Swoon Squad: A Romance TBR Book Club
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center C
description:

Swoon Squad is a romance-centered book club with a twist. Instead of everyone reading the same assigned title, we choose a monthly trope and invite you to pick any book that fits the theme! Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. Low Pressure, High Fun: No more scrambling to finish a specific book you might not even like. Read at your own pace and bring your honest thoughts! title: Storm Science: The Real Meteorology Behind the Movies
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:

Kyle will be joining us live via Zoom on our big screen to dive deep into the science of our atmosphere.Designed specifically for adults who love to know how things work, this program will cover:🚗 Storm Chasing & Field Research: What it’s actually like to pursue severe thunderstorms and tornadoes in the field to study extreme conditions.🔮 Weather Forecasting: How meteorologists predict major weather events before they hit.❄️ Local Winter Storms: A look into the powerful winter weather systems that shape our local climate.🚨 Weather Safety: Understanding the critical differences between weather watches and warnings to keep you weather-ready.Bring your curiosity for a live Q&A session with Kyle following the presentation! 🗣️❓🎟️ Registration is recommended to ensure your seat in the room. Sign up today!

Dr. Robert Frick, historian and presenter, will share the stories and facts related to six events that significantly impacted the United States. #### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public

July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

title: Lancaster Scrapbooking & Papercrafting Monthly gathering
description:
Lancaster Scrapbooking, Cards & Papercrafts
Scrapbook, make cards, practice quilling, or paint!
Meeting on the third Tuesday, 6-10 p.m., at the Cozy Crop House. (Also meeting the next night, Wednesday, same time & place. You can come to one or both, and can leave your gear overnight.) A chance to meet & gather monthly with local scrapbookers & crafters, in an ideal crafting environment! Plenty of room to do your own thing while we socialize. Bring your own supplies & projects, or just sit back and relax with scrapping friends, and watch & learn a new technique.
Specific crafting events (eg. card classes, paint nights, etc) may be featured here as scheduled.
Bring snacks to share if you wish.
Meetup groups are charged a monthly administration fee which is currently paid in this group by a few members. VOLUNTARY donations of $1 or $2 into a group "kitty" will help us continue the group's open membership and online advertising. The rate it costs our _whole group_ is about $12/month for a 6-month commitment. Please do not feel you cannot come if you don't contribute--the fee is paid, and donations are voluntary to cover future fees.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

* A welcoming, inclusive environment

* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**

title: Lancaster Scrapbooking & Papercrafting Monthly gathering
description:
Lancaster Scrapbooking, Cards & Papercrafts
Scrapbook, make cards, practice quilling, or paint!
Meeting on the third Tuesday, 6-10 p.m., at the Cozy Crop House. (Also meeting the next night, Wednesday, same time & place. You can come to one or both, and can leave your gear overnight.) A chance to meet & gather monthly with local scrapbookers & crafters, in an ideal crafting environment! Plenty of room to do your own thing while we socialize. Bring your own supplies & projects, or just sit back and relax with scrapping friends, and watch & learn a new technique.
Specific crafting events (eg. card classes, paint nights, etc) may be featured here as scheduled.
Bring snacks to share if you wish.
Meetup groups are charged a monthly administration fee which is currently paid in this group by a few members. VOLUNTARY donations of $1 or $2 into a group "kitty" will help us continue the group's open membership and online advertising. The rate it costs our _whole group_ is about $12/month for a 6-month commitment. Please do not feel you cannot come if you don't contribute--the fee is paid, and donations are voluntary to cover future fees.
